transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, but... well, I work in production, on a line, and my supervisor told me I needed to come get some help. I really try to be a good worker, I promise, it's just... I guess I have this habit of leaving my station? Or, like, if we have a shift meeting, I'll just sort of pop up out of my seat when I'm definitely supposed to stay put. 

I don't mean to be disruptive or anything! It's just like my body takes off before I even think about it. But my boss says it's becoming a safety problem on the floor... which I totally get, and I really want to fix it so I don't cause any issues for them. Is that the kind of thing I should be telling you?

When you're sitting still at your workstation and trying not to move, do you feel like your legs or body are moving on their own, or does the urge to get up only happen when you're trying to stay in one place?

Um, that's a really good question. It's not exactly that my body moves totally on its own, I don't think? It's more like... well, if I'm trying really, really hard to stay seated, like when we have to sit for a certification class or a long safety meeting, I just... I sort of have to do *something* with my hands or my legs. 

I try to keep it small, I promise, but my foot will just be bouncing, or I'll catch myself clicking a pen over and over, or picking at my sleeves. I guess I end up shifting around in my chair a lot, too. Sometimes I do it so much that the people next to me actually ask me to stop... which is really embarrassing. I hate bothering my coworkers, I really do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering what you were asking.

When you're not at work—like at home watching TV or having dinner with family—do you find yourself fidgeting and moving around a lot, or is this mainly something that happens when you're supposed to stay still for work?

Um, well... I guess it happens at home, too? But it's really not that bad, I promise. Like, if I'm watching TV, I might just get up to grab a drink, or maybe fold some laundry while the show is on. I just like to be helpful and keep things tidy, you know? 

I mean, my family does joke sometimes that I'm like a little tornado, always moving around during dinner or getting up to clear plates before everyone is completely finished. But I don't think it bothers them too much? I just want to make sure everyone has what they need. I try really hard to sit and watch a whole movie with them, I just... sometimes I need a little break to stretch my legs. Is that okay? I hope that's a normal thing to do.
Going back to when you were a kid in school, did you have this same trouble with fidgeting and needing to move around in your classroom, or is this something that's more of a recent problem for you?

Um, well... I guess it's not super recent? I mean, I really don't want to sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I always wanted to be good for my teachers. But, yeah, even back in elementary school, I was kind of the one who... well, I had a hard time staying in my seat. 

I'd get these notes sent home sometimes because I'd be wandering around the room, or I guess I'd talk over the teacher or blurt things out without raising my hand. I really didn't mean to be disrespectful, I promise! I just got so excited about what we were learning, or I'd think of an answer and it would just pop out. I hope you don't think I was a troublemaker. I really did try my best to be a good student... is it bad that I've always been like this?

Besides the fidgeting and moving around, do you find it hard to focus or concentrate on things? Like, do you have trouble keeping your attention on a task, or do you often lose track of what you're supposed to be doing?

Um, well... I really try my best to pay attention, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm slacking off at work or anything. It's just... sometimes, yeah, I guess it can be a little hard? 

Like, when I have to do the inventory logs or read through the CNC training pages... I always start out really focused, wanting to do a good job. But after a few minutes, it's like... I don't know, the numbers and words just sort of blur together? And then I realize I didn't actually take any of it in, so I have to keep going back and re-reading the same parts. I always get it done eventually, though! I just... I feel really bad that it takes me longer sometimes. Is that... is that what you mean by trouble focusing? I hope that's an okay answer.
When you get an idea or feel an urge to do something, do you usually act on it right away without thinking it through first? Or are you able to stop and think before you do things?

Um... I'm not really sure I do that? I mean, I always try to be really careful, especially on the production floor at work. I know safety is super important, so I wouldn't just do something out of nowhere without thinking. I really try to be responsible. 

I guess if I get an idea, I try my best to stop and think it through first, because I really don't want to make any mistakes or get in trouble with my supervisor. So... I haven't really noticed that being a problem for me? I hope that makes sense. I just always want to make sure I'm doing things the right way, you know? Is that a good thing?
When you're given a task or project to do—like at work or at home—do you have trouble getting started on it, or do you sometimes forget what you were supposed to be doing in the first place?

Um, well... I definitely don't want you to think I'm lazy or that I don't care about my job! I really, really try to be on top of everything. I'm always eager to get started when my supervisor gives me a project. 

But... I guess sometimes I do have a little trouble remembering every single little detail? Like, I'll forget normal stuff sometimes... maybe I'll forget to check off a step on the daily checklist, or I won't remember to answer a text from my supervisor right away. Or sometimes I'll realize I forgot my safety glasses in my locker and have to run back for them. 

I always feel so terrible when it happens because I worry it makes it look like I'm not taking things seriously, or like I just don't care. But I promise I do care! I really try to keep track of everything. I just... things slip my mind sometimes. Is it normal to be a little forgetful like that? I really hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad employee.

When you were in high school or middle school, did teachers or your parents ever mention anything to you about the fidgeting, trouble focusing, or forgetting things we've been talking about? Or is that something that started more recently?

Um... well... I hope you don't think I was a bad kid or anything! I really always wanted my teachers to like me, and I tried so hard to be good. But... yeah, I guess it's not a new thing. 

Even back in elementary school, I was kind of... well, they said I was a handful. I was the kid who just couldn't seem to stay in my seat, no matter how hard I tried to sit still. And I'd get so excited about things that I'd end up talking over the teacher, or just blurting out answers without raising my hand. I didn't mean to be disrespectful, I promise! I just... the words would come out before I could stop them. 

My parents used to get notes sent home a lot because I'd wander around the room during quiet time. I always felt so ashamed when that happened because I hated getting in trouble and disappointing my parents and teachers. I really did want to be a good student. Does... does that make sense? I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a troublemaker. I really wasn't trying to be!

You mentioned your supervisor sent you here because of the fidgeting and moving around at work. Besides work, has this fidgeting or trouble focusing caused any real problems for you in other areas of your life—like with relationships, school, or things you wanted to accomplish?

Um... well... I really, really hope you don't think I'm a bad person or a terrible employee for saying this... but I guess it has caused some issues at work. I try so hard, I really do, but... my supervisors have actually written me up a couple of times. It was for some safety and production things... just because I was moving around when I shouldn't have been, or I lost track of what I was doing. 

I felt so awful about it. I really want to get my certification, and I'm worried this might put all those plans at risk. And... I think maybe some of my coworkers get a little frustrated with me? Like, sometimes they seem less willing to partner with me when we have to do handoffs on the floor. 

I hate thinking that I'm making their jobs harder. I always want to be a good team player and pull my weight, you know? I just... I don't mean to mess things up. Is it okay that I told you that? I just really want to fix this so I can be the kind of worker they need me to be.
